title: A linear neighbor-flux fit retains a 20 ppm phase component in KIC 10001893 Kepler Q11 to Q17 aperture data
abstract: We test whether measured flux of KIC 10001898 explains the known 19.48-hour component of nearby KIC 10001893. We match 48,006 exposures in 14 Kepler release-25 quarters and fit neighbor flux with separate quarter coefficients. At the fixed prior frequency of 14.261300 microHz, an early phase sets the later test. With 3-day trends and 6-day noise blocks, the Q11 to Q17 aperture-flux component changes from 19.59 +/- 6.52 to 19.74 +/- 6.51 ppm. The paired change is +0.15 +/- 1.49 ppm. Six-day trends and corrected flux also give small changes. At least 99.56 percent of harmonic design power remains. The tested linear neighbor model does not remove the later component. This does not contradict earlier custom pixel extraction: standard apertures mix the stars, measured neighbor noise can bias the fit, and the coefficient may vary with frequency. Errors are conditional on the historical frequency, early phase and measured covariate. No planet or new source is confirmed. Original code, aggregate results, a figure, exact hashes and separate-scratch retrieval steps are included.

display.caption: Later early-phase components before and after a joint neighbor-flux fit. Bars are 1.96 times conditional errors from 6-day noise blocks. Flux products share exposures. Panels use different scales.
